facts.text: Saint Louisville was originally called Lewisville, named after Lautzenheiser's son Lewis, before changing its spelling to avoid confusion with another Ohio town.
The Pittsburgh, Fort Wayne and Chicago Railway reached Saint Louisville in 1852, sparking a boom that outpaced nearby Harrisburg.
Saint Louisville’s historic downtown district stretches roughly from Chapel Street to Center Court, featuring landmarks like Saint Louis Catholic Church built in 1870.
The town’s first public street lights—twelve oil burners—illuminated downtown for Christmas 1884, marking a milestone in local modernization.
A public water system was installed in 1894, followed by a sewage system in 1910, laying the groundwork for Saint Louisville’s modern infrastructure.
